newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-NEW ZEALAND BARBARIANS TOO STRONG FOR ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NEW ZEALAND BARBARIANS TOO STRONG FOR ENGLAND.

text.p: England missed their chance to gain some revenge for last year's World Cup thrashing by the All Blacks when they were beaten 34-19 by the New Zealand Barbarians at Twickenham on Saturday.

The home side led 19-13 early in the second half but were undone by a late New Zealand surge which produced 15 points in the last seven minutes of a hard-fought match celebrating the Rugby Football Union's 125th anniversary.

Auckland fly-half Carlos Spencer, pressed into second-half action as a replacement for Andrew Mehrtens, proved the game's decisive figure by kicking two penalties and a conversion and scoring a wonderful individual try to seal victory.
England had held a slightly fortunate 9-6 lead at halftime but were behind again within 50 seconds of the restart when flanker Andrew Blowers raced over to capitalise on a break by Andrew Mehrtens.
Two tries in five minutes from winger Jon Sleightholme and full-back Tim Stimpson put them back in front but the New Zealanders were worthy winners in the end.
